questions.question: What following distance should you normally maintain?
questions.explanation: In normal conditions, keep at least two seconds of distance between you and the vehicle in front of you. Increase this distance if conditions are poor.

questions.question: How should you cross railroad tracks that run parallel to the road?

options.text: Cross the tracks at a 90-degree angle.
Avoid crossing the tracks for any reason.
Cross the tracks at a 45-degree angle or steeper.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cross the tracks at a 45-degree angle or steeper.
questions.explanation: To cross railroad tracks safely, position yourself to cross at least at a 45-degree angle. Then make a quick, sharp turn. Crossing slowly or at a shallow angle can catch your tires and cause you to lose control.

questions.question: How should you swerve on a motorcycle?

options.text: Push the handgrip in the direction you want to turn.
Push the handgrip in the opposite direction of the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Push the handgrip in the direction you want to turn.
questions.explanation: To swerve, push the handgrip on the side where you want to go. To swerve left, push the left handgrip, then the right to straighten. To swerve right, push the right handgrip, then the left.

questions.question: The center of a lane often has an oily strip. Is this area safe for motorcyclists?

options.text: Usually safe, unless the road is wet.
Usually safe, unless it is sunny outside.
Always safe, no matter the weather conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Usually safe, unless the road is wet.
questions.explanation: Oil from cars collects in the center of traffic lanes. In dry conditions, this area usually has enough grip for motorcycles. When the road is wet, however, this oily strip becomes slippery. Since the strip is only about two feet wide, you can often ride around it and still stay in the center of your lane.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a cause of motorcycle wobble?
questions.explanation: Most wobbles come from improper loading, unsuitable accessories, or incorrect tire pressure. Do not try to speed up to stop a wobble.

questions.question: What should you do when another vehicle passes you from behind?

options.text: Use the left portion of your lane.
Use the center portion of your lane.
Use the right portion of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the center portion of your lane.
questions.explanation: When being passed, the center of your lane is safest. Riding on the side nearest the passing vehicle increases collision risk. Riding on the far side can make the driver try to return to your lane too soon.

questions.question: What is required to swerve a motorcycle safely?

options.text: You should swerve to avoid hazards on slippery roads.

questions.explanation: Swerving is a quick maneuver that needs lots of traction to work safely. Do not swerve suddenly on slippery surfaces.

questions.question: When should you increase your following distance?

options.text: When you can see the roadway through vehicles ahead.
When weather is clear and pleasant.

questions.explanation: Although two seconds is usually enough, increase your following distance when you need more space to stop, such as in bad weather. Also increase it at night, when you cannot see ahead clearly, or when traffic is heavy.

questions.question: Which sign shape is rectangular?
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs like speed limit signs are rectangular with white backgrounds and black letters or symbols. You must follow the rules shown on these signs.

questions.question: How many paths of travel does each traffic lane provide for a motorcyclist?
questions.explanation: Each traffic lane offers three paths for motorcyclists: the left side, the center, and the right side of the lane.

questions.question: For an eye or face shield to work well, it must:

options.text: Block all air from passing through.
Not allow eyeglasses to fit underneath.

questions.explanation: A good eye or face shield must fasten securely. It should also be scratch-free, resist penetration, allow clear views to the sides, let air pass through to prevent fogging, and have room for eyeglasses or sunglasses if needed.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT a good safety tip?

options.text: Slow down to a safe speed before turning.
Lean in the direction you are turning.
Do not drag your feet on the road.

questions.explanation: Slow to a safe speed before turning and lean in the direction of the turn. Do not drag your feet on the road because they could catch and cause you to lose control. Always watch for other traffic on the road.

questions.question: Because motorcycles are small, they may appear to be:

options.text: Moving faster than they actually are.
Moving slower than they actually are.
Not moving when they actually are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Moving faster than they actually are.
questions.explanation: Because of their small size, motorcycles may look like they are moving faster than they really are.

questions.question: To be more visible at an intersection, you should:

options.text: Try to make eye contact with other drivers.
Reduce the space between you and other vehicles.

questions.explanation: Keep your headlight on to increase visibility at intersections. Ride in a lane position that makes it easy for oncoming traffic to see you. Keep space around you so you can react if needed. Do not assume another driver sees you, even if you make eye contact.

questions.question: How many crashes between motorcycles and cars are caused by the driver not properly yielding to the rider?
questions.explanation: More than half of all crashes between motorcycles and cars happen because the driver fails to properly yield the right-of-way to the motorcycle rider.

questions.question: The center of a lane:

options.text: Is always the best place to ride a motorcycle.
Often has oil and grease, but is usually safe for riding.
Often has oil and grease, and is never safe for riding.
Is the smoothest part of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Often has oil and grease, but is usually safe for riding.
questions.explanation: Oil from cars collects in a strip down the center of each lane. On dry roads, this area usually has enough grip for safe riding. However, avoid riding on large buildups of oil and grease, which are common at busy intersections and toll booths.

questions.question: Most motorcycle crashes happen:
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen on trips shorter than five miles at speeds slower than 30 mph.

questions.question: Which sign is yellow with black letters or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road hazards and conditions.

questions.question: To avoid fatigue on a long ride, you should do all of the following EXCEPT:

options.text: Limit how far you ride each day.

questions.explanation: To prevent fatigue while riding, dress to protect yourself from wind and rain. Ride no more than about six hours per day and take a break at least every two hours. Do not use artificial stimulants because you may become very tired when they wear off.

questions.question: If a passing vehicle creates a wind blast that hits you, you will have the most room to react if you are riding:

options.text: In the left part of the lane.
In the center of the lane.
In the right part of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the center of the lane.
questions.explanation: If you are in the middle of your lane, you have the most room to recover if a wind blast from a passing vehicle affects your control.

questions.question: Which idea should NOT be used when planning a long group ride?

options.text: Plan travel segment lengths based on the least experienced rider.
Skip breaks so riders reach their destination faster.
Place inexperienced riders behind the leaders.

questions.correctAnswerText: Skip breaks so riders reach their destination faster.
questions.explanation: Plan route length based on the least experienced rider's skill level. Take regular breaks to prevent fatigue. Place inexperienced riders behind leaders so experienced riders can watch them. Ride in a staggered formation.

questions.question: How do you regain control if your rear tire locks up?

options.text: Try to speed up while braking.

questions.explanation: Release the rear brake to regain control of a locked rear wheel. If you lock the rear brake on good pavement, you can keep it locked until you stop completely.

questions.question: Small vehicles can look ______ and seem to move ______ than they really are.
questions.explanation: Small vehicles like motorcycles appear farther away and moving slower than they actually are. This makes it hard to judge their real distance and speed.

questions.question: As the operator, what should you NOT tell your passenger to do?

options.text: Get on after the engine starts.
Sit as far forward as possible.
Keep a large space between themselves and you.
Keep their legs away from the muffler and chains.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep a large space between themselves and you.
questions.explanation: Tell your passenger to mount after the engine starts. They should sit forward without crowding you and hold the handholds or your waist. They should keep their legs away from the muffler, chains, and moving parts.

questions.question: When are you least likely to see a deer or moose?
questions.explanation: Deer and moose are most active during late evening, night, and early morning hours.
